p.instruction: Put these sentences from You Can Say No in the order printed.
shuffled: Saying no to frivolities helps us to affirm our person as a unique individual, and increases our confidence and trust in God (Nehemiah 2:20).

It also creates safe and healthy boundaries, guides and helps us prioritise as we separate our needs from our wants, keeps us focused, helps us to be stable and free from needless pressure of satisfying human beings and being men-pleasers.
The power to say no to any negativity is possible because humans are choice creatures with the willpower to make planned selections.

We can say no to sin (Romans 6:12-14), temptation (1Corinthians 10:13; Matthew 26:41), negative influences (1 Peter 5:8-9), fears and doubts (Isaiah 41:10, James 1:6), worldly pleasures (James 4:4; 1 John 2:15-16), denial of faith (2 Timothy 2:12; Matthew 10:32-33), evil company (Proverbs 1:10), bitterness (Hebrews 12:15), laziness (Proverbs 18:9; 21:25), gluttony (Proverbs 23:20-21), past achievements (Philippians 3:13-14) and prayerlessness and lack of the study of God’s word (Psalm 119:147-148).
